title: Ducks Lock In Gauthier with Six-Year, $81M Extension Before CBA Deadline
dek: The Anaheim Ducks signed left wing Cutter Gauthier to a six-year, $81 million extension on September 16, keeping him through 2031-32. The deal was structured with approximately $69.5 million in signing bonuses before the new collective bargaining agreement took effect, allowing front-loading not possible under the new labor terms.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Gauthier's $81M extension was signed before the new CBA kicked in on September 16, 2026, enabling heavy front-loading with $69.5M in signing bonuses, including $18.6M in Year 1.
bottom_line: Gauthier's extension resolves one of Anaheim's major offseason priorities and locks in the left wing before tighter CBA restrictions take hold. The Ducks' minimal remaining cap flexibility will determine whether this structure supports a competitive roster for the six-year commitment.
body: The Anaheim Ducks signed left wing Cutter Gauthier to a six-year, $81 million extension on September 16, keeping him through the 2031-32 season. The timing was critical: the deal closed before the new collective bargaining agreement took effect the same day, allowing the Ducks to structure the contract with signing bonuses in ways the new labor terms would not permit.

Gauthier, 22, becomes the second-highest paid player on the roster behind Leo Carlsson's $18 million average annual value. According to Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman, roughly $69.5 million of the $81 million total comprises signing bonuses. Per ESPN's Emily Kaplan, $18.6 million of that signing-bonus pool arrives in Year 1, front-loading cash in the early years of the deal.

The extension buys Gauthier one year of unrestricted free agency. General manager Pat Verbeek said in a statement: "We are pleased to get Cutter signed to a long-term deal and have him in camp on time. He's a major part of our young core, a pure goal-scoring talent that will continue progressing into an elite NHL player." Gauthier stated: "This is a very exciting day for my family and me. I'm so pleased to be able to sign long term with the Ducks and be part of what I believe is a great future."

Gauthier's camp had declined a four-year, $13 million average annual value offer last month, according to reporting. The financial landscape for young star forwards has shifted markedly following Leo Carlsson's offer sheet from Philadelphia, Connor Bedard, Macklin Celebrini, and Cale Makar's recent major extensions. Smaller deals signed by players like the Ducks' Pavel Mintyukov and the Boston Bruins' Fraser Minten, combined with continued salary-cap growth, have shifted leverage toward players seeking larger compensation.

To free cap space for the extension, the Ducks terminated Chris Kreider's contract the week before the Gauthier deal was announced, opening $6.5 million in room. The team's cap constraints remain narrow despite that move; the Ducks expect to place Troy Terry on long-term injured reserve (out 2-3 months after hip surgery) to create additional short-term relief. A shortened training camp and preseason leaves limited preparation time, though Anaheim's later season-opening date provides a modest scheduling advantage.
